title_en: Li Xuehua and Fan Yang v. Fan Zuye and Teng Ying — inheritance dispute
ruling_gist_en: During the subsistence of a marital relationship, after both parties have mutually agreed to use another person's sperm for artificial insemination and the wife becomes pregnant, if the husband later reconsents, he must obtain the wife's consent. Where the husband dies without reaching a consensus, and thereafter the child is born, although the child has no biological relationship with the husband, the child shall still be regarded as a legitimate child of the marriage. If the husband, in his will, fails to reserve the necessary share of the estate for the child, such disposition violates the provisions of Article 19 of the Inheritance Law, and that part of the will is invalid.
keywords_en: Civil; inheritance dispute; first instance; grassroots people's court; Jiangsu Province; natural person; Inheritance Law; inheritance rights of children born through artificial insemination; validity of will; system of compulsory share; partial support; artificial insemination; will; partition of estate; good faith; Teng Ying inheritance dispute
full_text_en:
Li Xuehua and Fan Yang v. Fan Zuye and Teng Ying — inheritance dispute

Ruling Summary

During the existence of the marital relationship, where both spouses unanimously agreed to use another person's sperm for artificial insemination resulting in the wife's pregnancy, the husband may only withdraw his consent with the wife's agreement. Where the husband dies before an agreement is reached, and a child is subsequently born, the child shall be regarded as a legitimate child of both spouses even though the child has no blood relationship with the husband. Where the husband, in his will, fails to reserve a necessary share of the estate for such child, such failure is inconsistent with Article 19 of the Inheritance Law, and the relevant part of the will is invalid.

Plaintiffs: Li Xuehua, female, 42 years old, unemployed, residing at Room 306, Anjuli, Qinhuai District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Plaintiff: Fan Yang, male, 2 years old, son of Li Xuehua, residing at the same address as Li Xuehua.

Legal Representative: Li Xuehua (personal details as above).

Defendants: Fan Zuye, male, 72 years old, retired worker, residing at Room 305, Anjuli, Qinhuai District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Teng Ying, female, 69 years old, retired worker, wife of Fan Zuye, residing at the same address as Fan Zuye.

The plaintiffs, Li Xuehua and Fan Yang, instituted an action in the Qinhuai District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, against the defendants, Fan Zuye and Teng Ying, concerning a dispute over division of property and inheritance.

Plaintiff Li Xuehua alleged: The house located at Room 306, Anjuli, Nanjing, is the jointly owned property of the plaintiff Li Xuehua and the decedent, Fan Shunxiang. After Fan Shunxiang died of illness, the plaintiff Fan Yang was born. The estate of Fan Shunxiang should be inherited jointly by the statutory heirs: the wife Li Xuehua, the son Fan Yang, and the parents of Fan Shunxiang, i.e., the defendants Fan Zuye and Teng Ying. The plaintiffs have attempted to negotiate the division of the estate with the defendants on multiple occasions without reaching an agreement, and therefore request the court to resolve this dispute over property division and inheritance. In dividing the property, consideration should be given to the specific circumstances that Fan Zuye and Teng Ying have their own housing and retirement pensions, whereas Li Xuehua has no steady income and must raise a young child, and thus Li Xuehua and Fan Yang should be given favorable consideration.

The plaintiff Li Xuehua submitted the following evidence:

1. Marriage certificate, to prove the marital relationship between Li Xuehua and Fan Shunxiang;
2. Public housing sales contract, payment receipt, house ownership certificate, and state-owned land use certificate, to prove that Room 306, Anjuli was a house purchased in the name of Fan Shunxiang during the existence of the marital relationship between Fan Shunxiang and Li Xuehua;
3. Application for artificial insemination for infertile couples and artificial insemination agreement, to prove that Li Xuehua became pregnant through artificial insemination with the signed consent of Fan Shunxiang, and that the child born, Fan Yang, is a lawful heir of Fan Shunxiang;
4. Death and funeral certificate for residents, to prove that Fan Shunxiang died of illness on May 23, 2004;
5. Receipts and IOUs, to prove that when Fan Shunxiang and Li Xuehua purchased the house, they borrowed RMB 10,000 from Fan Zuye and Teng Ying, and repaid RMB 3,300 on March 1, 2005.

The defendants, Fan Zuye and Teng Ying, argued: First, Room 306, Anjuli was a public house allocated by the government to the Fan family as compensation following the demolition of the Fan family's private house; although this house was purchased in the name of Fan Shunxiang, the two defendants contributed RMB 10,000 at the time of purchase, accounting for two-thirds of the total purchase price. Therefore, this house is not the jointly owned property of Fan Shunxiang and Li Xuehua, but rather family property of the Fan family, and the two defendants at least have a two-thirds property right in the house. Second, Fan Shunxiang left a will during his lifetime, explicitly gifting Room 306, Anjuli to the two defendants, and therefore statutory inheritance does not apply to this property. Third, the child born to Li Xuehua has no blood relationship with Fan Shunxiang; although Fan Shunxiang signed to consent to the pregnancy through artificial insemination, after learning that he had cancer, he expressed to Li Xuehua that he did not want the child, and it was not too late at that time to have an abortion; Li Xuehua insisted on giving birth to this child, and she should naturally be responsible for him; Fan Shunxiang stated in his will that he did not want this child born through artificial insemination, and this wish should be respected, so this child cannot be listed as an heir of Fan Shunxiang. Fourth, Li Xuehua claims to be the wife of Fan Shunxiang, but during Fan Shunxiang's critical illness, she did not provide money for his medical treatment and failed to fulfill her spousal duty of support, and therefore she has no right to inherit the real property left by Fan Shunxiang; this property should be disposed of according to Fan Shunxiang's will. Fifth, during his lifetime, Fan Shunxiang borrowed RMB 8,500 from Teng Ying for the purpose of opening a business; at the time of Fan Shunxiang's death, he left a large sum of deposits which are now held by Li Xuehua; Li Xuehua only seeks to inherit the real property but refuses to divide the deposits she holds or to use them to repay Fan Shunxiang's debts, which is unfair; the deposits left by Fan Shunxiang should be used to satisfy the debts he left, and the remainder should be dealt with according to statutory inheritance.

The defendants, Fan Zuye and Teng Ying, submitted the following evidence:

1. A will handwritten by Fan Shunxiang in the hospital on May 20, 2004, stating: "1. Regarding the child conceived through artificial insemination (not my sperm), I firmly reject it; 2. The house allocated after the demolition of the private house in 1984, located at Room 306, Anjuli, Qinhuai District, which was purchased in my name under the housing reform policy with a contribution of RMB 15,000 from my mother at that time, is gifted to my parents, Fan Zuye and Teng Ying, and no one may object."
2. A will dictated on May 22, 2004, and written by Yuan Moumou, a staff member of a certain legal service office, the main content of which is: Testator Fan Shunxiang, I have suffered from cancer for many years, and my condition is currently worsening. I am now hospitalized for treatment. Because my mother has given so much to me, to repay her kindness, while my mind is still clear, I make the following will: First, the small house located at Room 306, Anjuli, Qinhuai District, Nanjing, is a property purchased with ownership rights in 2003 in my name but with money from my mother. After my death, my entire share of the property rights shall be inherited by my mother. Second, in 2001, I borrowed RMB 8,500 from my mother for business purposes. Currently, I have deposits of about RMB 60,000 at the Agricultural Bank of China. After my death, my half, i.e., RMB 30,000, shall be inherited by my mother.
3. An IOU written by Fan Shunxiang, stating: "Fan Shunxiang borrowed RMB 8,500 from mother for opening a shop, to be repaid when money is available. Fan Shunxiang, March 12, 2001."
4. A note written by Fan Shunxiang, the main content of which is: "Li Xuehua, the RMB 25,000 I earned from driving a delivery truck is with you. Now I am hospitalized and need money. Please bring it out for me to use. Fan Shunxiang, May 21, 2004."

The court conducted examination of evidence. During the examination, the parties disputed the following issues concerning the determination of facts: 1. Was Room 306, Anjuli purchased by the couple Fan Shunxiang and Li Xuehua, or was it purchased jointly by Fan Shunxiang and the defendants Fan Zuye and Teng Ying? 2. Did Li Xuehua fulfill her spousal duty of support during Fan Shunxiang's illness? 3. Did Fan Shunxiang leave any deposits after his death, and what was the amount? 4. Did Fan Shunxiang borrow money from Teng Ying during his lifetime for business operations?

Regarding the first issue, plaintiff Li Xuehua stated: The payment receipt, bills, IOUs, and receipts prove that the purchase price of RMB 14,582.16 was paid entirely by Fan Shunxiang alone, of which RMB 10,000 was borrowed from the two defendants, not a joint contribution to the purchase; after Fan Shunxiang's death, the borrowed purchase money was repaid by me to the two defendants, and the two defendants accepted this money; their current claim of joint contribution to the purchase has no factual basis. The defendants Fan Zuye and Teng Ying argued: Both Fan Shunxiang's handwritten will and the dictated will confirm that the house was purchased with joint contributions; later, when resolving the dispute at the police station, out of respect for the police station's mediation opinion, the two defendants accepted the money paid by the plaintiff; this was done to resolve the conflict and does not mean that the existence of the loan is acknowledged. The court found: The IOUs and receipts prove the existence of the loan, and the loan was repaid upon the demand of the two defendants. In his handwritten will and dictated will, Fan Shunxiang stated that the entire purchase price of RMB 150,000 was contributed by his mother Teng Ying, which is inconsistent both with the fact that the IOUs and receipts prove a loan of RMB 10,000 and with the claim of Fan Zuye and Teng Ying that they contributed RMB 10,000 for a joint purchase. Moreover, the dictated will not only incorrectly writes the house number as Room 305, Anjuli for the inherited real property, but also fails to meet the requirement that the will be dictated in the presence of two or more witnesses, written by one of them, and signed by the writer, the other witnesses, and the testator, as required by Article 17, Paragraph 3 of the Inheritance Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Inheritance Law") regarding the formal requirements for a dictated will; therefore, it cannot be used as evidence.

Regarding the second issue. The defendants Fan Zuye and Teng Ying claimed: After Fan Shunxiang was diagnosed with cancer and the hospital issued a critical illness notice, plaintiff Li Xuehua immediately showed the notice to Fan Shunxiang, causing him great psychological stress and a rapid deterioration of his condition; during Fan Shunxiang's critical illness, he asked Li Xuehua to provide money for his treatment, even kneeling and begging her for money, but Li Xuehua refused to provide any money, failing to fulfill her spousal duty of support; these actions by Li Xuehua were known to the doctors, and the court should investigate the doctors. Li Xuehua stated that the claims of Fan Zuye and Teng Ying were untrue. Upon the application of Fan Zuye and Teng Ying, the court conducted an investigation by interviewing Fan Shunxiang's attending physician at the hospital. According to the physician, during Fan Shunxiang's hospitalization, Li Xuehua, like Fan Shunxiang's sister, was at the hospital almost every day caring for the patient, although she was not very talkative; after the critical illness notice was issued, the physician heard from Fan Shunxiang's sister that Li Xuehua had shown the notice to Fan Shunxiang; as to whether Li Xuehua actually showed the notice to Fan Shunxiang and whether Fan Shunxiang begged Li Xuehua for money, the physician did not know. Therefore, the court did not accept the claim of Fan Zuye and Teng Ying that Li Xuehua failed to fulfill her spousal duty of support.

Regarding the third issue. The defendants Fan Zuye and Teng Ying claimed that Fan Shunxiang left a large sum of deposits at the time of his death, and this sum is now held by plaintiff Li Xuehua. Li Xuehua admitted that, before Fan Shunxiang fell ill, the deposits she held amounted to RMB 54,800, but after deducting Fan Shunxiang's medical expenses, funeral expenses, the repayment of the house loan, and the expenses for giving birth to and raising Fan Yang, as well as the lawyer's fees and prepaid litigation costs for this case, only RMB 9,000 remain. Fan Zuye and Teng Ying acknowledged that the medical expenses, funeral expenses, house loan repayment, and childbirth expenses could be deducted from the deposits, but did not acknowledge the other expenses. The court found: The expenses claimed by Li Xuehua, such as medical expenses, funeral expenses, house loan repayment, and childbirth expenses, were all payments made for the common family living and are supported by withdrawal slips, hospital receipts, cemetery certificates, etc. They can be deducted from the joint deposits of the spouses. Other items either have not yet been incurred or are not expenses for common family living and should not be deducted from the joint deposits. Accordingly, the court determined that the joint deposits held by Li Xuehua amount to RMB 18,705.4.

Regarding the fourth issue. Defendant Teng Ying claimed: On March 12, 2001, Fan Shunxiang borrowed RMB 8,500 from her for the purpose of opening a shop, as evidenced by an IOU written by Fan Shunxiang. Plaintiff Li Xuehua stated: When Fan Shunxiang opened the shop, he received assistance from the neighborhood committee and did not need to borrow money for operations; although the IOU was written by Fan Shunxiang, Fan Shunxiang had clearly shown a tendency to favor his parents' interests before his death, and therefore the loan reflected in the IOU is not true. The court found: The couple Fan Shunxiang and Li Xuehua did operate a shop, which required capital. Li Xuehua's assertion that the shop did not need a loan is untenable, as she could not identify the source of the capital. Teng Ying's claim that Fan Shunxiang borrowed RMB 8,500 from her for the shop, supported by the IOU written by Fan Shunxiang, should be recognized as fact.

After examination and verification of evidence, the Qinhuai District People's Court of Nanjing found the following facts:

On March 3, 1998, plaintiff Li Xuehua married Fan Shunxiang, the son of defendants Fan Zuye and Teng Ying.

On August 27, 2002, Fan Shunxiang signed a "Nanjing Municipal Directly Managed Public Housing Sales Contract" with the Qinhuai District Real Estate Management Company to purchase Room 306, with a construction area of 45.08 square meters, located at Anjuli, Qinhuai District, Nanjing. On the same day, Fan Shunxiang paid the purchase price of RMB 14,582.16, of which RMB 10,000 was borrowed from the defendants Fan Zuye and Teng Ying. In September of the same year, Fan Shunxiang obtained the house ownership certificate and state-owned land use certificate in his own name. In March and October 2005, plaintiff Li Xuehua repaid the RMB 10,000 loan to Fan Zuye and Teng Ying in two installments. In March 2006, commissioned by the court, Nanjing Mainland Real Estate Appraisers Co., Ltd. appraised Room 306, Anjuli, with the current market value assessed at RMB 193,000.

On January 30, 2004, plaintiff Li Xuehua and Fan Shunxiang jointly signed an artificial insemination agreement with the Reproductive Genetics Center of Nanjing General Hospital of Nanjing Military Command. Through artificial insemination, Li Xuehua gave birth to a son on October 22, 2004, named Fan Yang.

In April 2004, Fan Shunxiang was hospitalized due to illness. On May 20, 2004, Fan Shunxiang made a handwritten will in the hospital. He died on May 23, 2004.

It was further found: The defendants Fan Zuye and Teng Ying currently reside in Room 305, Anjuli, with the owner of that property being Fan Zuye. Both Fan Zuye and Teng Ying receive retirement pensions. In March 2001, Fan Shunxiang borrowed RMB 8,500 from Teng Ying to open a shop. Plaintiff Li Xuehua is unemployed, receives a minimum subsistence allowance each month, and has irregular income from part-time work. She currently holds joint deposits of RMB 18,705.4 from the marital relationship.

The issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Can Fan Yang be considered an heir of Fan Shunxiang? 2. Given that Fan Shunxiang left a will, how should the property in Room 306, Anjuli be divided and inherited? 3. How should the deposits held by Li Xuehua be disposed of?

The Qinhuai District People's Court of Nanjing held:

Regarding disputed issue 1. In its Reply dated July 8, 1991, concerning How to Determine the Legal Status of Children Born Through Artificial Insemination After Divorce, the Supreme People's Court stipulated: "Where both spouses, during the existence of the marital relationship, unanimously consent to artificial insemination, the child born as a result shall be regarded as a legitimate child of both spouses, and the rights and obligations between parents and children shall be governed by the relevant provisions of the Marriage Law." Since Fan Shunxiang was infertile, he signed to consent to the hospital performing artificial insemination on his wife, plaintiff Li Xuehua, thereby expressing his intention to obtain a child with Li Xuehua through artificial insemination. As long as both spouses consent to having a child through artificial insemination, the child born shall be regarded as a legitimate child of both spouses, regardless of whether the child has a blood relationship with one or both spouses. Article 57 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "General Principles of Civil Law") provides: "A civil juristic act shall be legally binding from the time of its establishment. The actor may not alter or rescind it at will, except as provided by law or with the consent of the other party." Due to his illness, Fan Shunxiang had a change of heart regarding his signed consent to the artificial insemination procedure, but by that time his wife Li Xuehua was already pregnant. For Fan Shunxiang to withdraw his consent, he was required by law to obtain Li Xuehua's agreement. Without Li Xuehua's agreement, Fan Shunxiang's signature was legally binding and could not be unilaterally altered or rescinded at his sole will. Therefore, Fan Shunxiang's denial in his will of the father-son relationship with the fetus carried by Li Xuehua constitutes an invalid civil act. The plaintiff Fan Yang, born to Li Xuehua, is a lawful heir of Fan Shunxiang.

Regarding disputed issue 2. Article 5 of the Inheritance Law provides: "Inheritance shall, upon its commencement, be handled in accordance with the provisions of statutory inheritance; where there is a will, it shall be handled in accordance with testamentary succession or bequest; where there is a legacy-support agreement, it shall be handled in accordance with the agreement." Upon the death of the decedent Fan Shunxiang, inheritance commenced. Given that Fan Shunxiang left a will, this case shall be handled in accordance with testamentary succession.

Article 26 of the Inheritance Law provides: "Where property jointly owned by the spouses is divided as estate upon the death of one spouse, half of the jointly owned property shall first be allocated to the surviving spouse, and the remainder shall constitute the estate of the decedent." Article 38 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Inheritance Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where a will disposes of property belonging to the state, a collective, or any other person, that part of the will shall be deemed invalid." Room 306, Anjuli, registered in the name of the decedent Fan Shunxiang, has been found to be jointly owned property acquired during the existence of the marital relationship between Fan Shunxiang and plaintiff Li Xuehua. After Fan Shunxiang's death, half of this house shall belong to Li Xuehua, and the other half shall constitute Fan Shunxiang's estate. In his will, Fan Shunxiang disposed of the entire Room 306, Anjuli in favor of his parents, thereby infringing upon Li Xuehua's property right in the house. This part of the will is invalid.

Article 19 of the Inheritance Law provides: "A will shall reserve a necessary share of the estate for an heir who lacks the capacity to work and has no source of income." Article 28 provides: "When dividing the estate, a share shall be reserved for the fetus. If the fetus is stillborn at birth, the reserved share shall be handled in accordance with statutory inheritance." The decedent Fan Shunxiang knew that plaintiff Li Xuehua, with his consent, had become pregnant through artificial insemination. However, when making his will, he gave all the real property he left to his parents for inheritance on the ground that he did not want this child. After Fan Shunxiang's death, plaintiff Fan Yang was born. Fan Yang is a legitimate child and lawful heir of Fan Shunxiang. After birth, he lacks the capacity to work and has no source of income. Fan Shunxiang failed to reserve a necessary share of the estate for Fan Yang in his will, which violates the provisions of Article 19 of the Inheritance Law. Therefore, in handling the estate, a necessary share shall first be reserved for Fan Yang, and the remaining portion may be disposed of according to the distribution principle set forth in the will.

The appraised value of Room 306, Anjuli is RMB 193,000. Considering the specific circumstances of this case, after setting aside the half of the jointly owned property to which plaintiff Li Xuehua is entitled, the remaining half, i.e., the real property valued at RMB 96,500, shall constitute the estate of the decedent Fan Shunxiang. From this real property left by Fan Shunxiang, one-third shall be reserved as the necessary share for plaintiff Fan Yang, and the remaining two-thirds shall be inherited jointly by the defendants Fan Zuye and Teng Ying. Considering the actual needs of each heir and their respective shares, Room 306, Anjuli shall belong to Li Xuehua, and Li Xuehua shall pay RMB 32,166.7 in cash as compensation to each of Fan Yang, Fan Zuye, and Teng Ying.

Regarding disputed issue 3. After the death of Fan Shunxiang, the remaining deposits from the marital relationship amount to RMB 18,705.4, held by plaintiff Li Xuehua. From these deposits, the joint debt of Fan Shunxiang and Li Xuehua to defendant Teng Ying in the amount of RMB 8,500 shall be repaid. After deducting Li Xuehua's half share of the jointly owned property, the remaining amount of RMB 5,102.7 constitutes Fan Shunxiang's estate. With respect to this portion of the estate, Fan Shunxiang did not mention it in his handwritten will, so it shall be handled in accordance with statutory inheritance. It shall be divided equally among the statutory first-order heirs, namely Li Xuehua, plaintiff Fan Yang, and the defendants Fan Zuye and Teng Ying, with each receiving RMB 1,275.7.

Accordingly, on April 20, 2006, the Qinhuai District People's Court of Nanjing rendered the following judgment:

1. The house located at Room 306, Anjuli, Qinhuai District, Nanjing shall belong to plaintiff Li Xuehua;
2. Within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, plaintiff Li Xuehua shall pay plaintiff Fan Yang RMB 33,442.4, which sum shall be kept by Fan Yang's legal representative, Li Xuehua;
3. Within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, plaintiff Li Xuehua shall pay defendant Fan Zuye RMB 33,442.4;
4. Within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, plaintiff Li Xuehua shall pay defendant Teng Ying RMB 41,942.4.

Court costs of RMB 3,764, appraisal fee of RMB 1,000, and investigation fee of RMB 100, totaling RMB 4,864, shall be borne by plaintiffs Li Xuehua and Fan Yang in the amount of RMB 2,918, and by defendants Fan Zuye and Teng Ying in the amount of RMB 1,946.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, neither party filed an appeal, and the judgment of first instance became legally effective.

(Editor's Note: This case involves privacy, so the names and addresses of the parties have been altered.)
